bull_bear.body: Debt repayment priority (Gateway gross debt down significantly); Dividend continuation; Organic capex for fleet modernization (EV) and terminal expansion; No near-term plans to increase stake in Snowman.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension (West Asia) suppressing EXIM volumes; Delay in DFC-JNPT last-mile connectivity; Regulatory/Legal delays for Jaipur ICD; Power tariff volatility impacting cold storage margins; Execution risk on domestic rail pivot.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic long-term, defensive short-term; Acknowledges 'wait-and-watch' on geopolitics; Transparent on margin headwinds being temporary (ramp-up phase); Committed to asset creation despite demand lull.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Snowman is actively reducing dry storage mix (currently 9-10%) to replace with higher-yield frozen cargo, which should structurally lift ASPs and margins once complete; The 'trading' segment is the sole driver of revenue growth but dilutes overall margins; Gateway is preparing for domestic rail dominance by absorbing upfront empty haulage costs now to secure future market share.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- scale: pan-India cold chain network spanning 45 warehouses in 21 cities that lets customers use Snowman as a single national platform rather than multiple regional providers — evidence: '45 warehouses across 21 cities with approximately 1.54 lakhs pallet capacity'; 'this network has taken many years to build and gives us a position that is difficult to replicate'
- licence/regulatory: certifications enabling handling of stringent temperature-sensitive categories such as pharmaceuticals — evidence: 'certified to internationally recognized GFSI standards, including BRCGS, FSSC 22000, and ISO 22000 for food safety and quality management' and 'ISO 14001 certification for our Environmental Management System'
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic headwinds and subdued freight demand — Continued macroeconomic headwinds, including inflationary pressures, global supply chain disruptions, and subdued consumer demand, present challenges in maintaining consistent freight volumes and network utilisation; sectors such as FMCG, pharmaceuticals, and automotive are increasingly sensitive to cost fluctuations and delays.
- Geopolitical instability affecting supply chain stability — Escalating geopolitical tensions globally pose a considerable risk to supply chain continuity, potentially triggering forced rerouting, increased commodity prices and inflationary pressures, impacting timely deliveries and cost structures.
- Fragmented, competitive, low-barrier-to-entry market — The Indian logistics landscape remains highly fragmented and competitive, with numerous unorganised players; this commoditised nature exerts downward pressure on pricing, especially in contract logistics and last-mile delivery, impacting profitability.
- Pricing pressure amid rising input costs — Escalating commodity prices, especially crude oil, have led to increased input costs, prompting clients to intensify cost control measures and resulting in heightened pricing pressure within contract logistics and last-mile delivery segments.
- Talent shortage and wage inflation — The sector faces ongoing challenges in sourcing and retaining skilled labor, particularly during peak demand periods; talent scarcity drives wage inflation, increasing operational costs and exerting upward pressure on pricing.
- Economic slowdown impacting freight demand — The prevailing economic slowdown has resulted in subdued consumption patterns, leading to reduced freight volumes and underutilization of logistics networks, with key sectors like FMCG and automotive experiencing disruptions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims to operate "the largest cold chain network in India, with 45 warehouses across 21 cities", supported by "Over 3 million+ sq. ft. of land area" and "600+ trucks ensuring a robust nationwide network".
- Incorporated in 1993; "Gateway Distriparks acquired a majority stake in 2006"; the deck cites "over 25 years of industry leadership and innovation in cold chain logistics" and lists Snowman as a "Subsidiary of Gateway Distriparks Limited".
- "Snowman is first Indian cold chain company to introduce 5PL services, which offer innovative and integrated solutions".
- Diversified end-market exposure across 13 industries served, including Dairy & Ice cream, FMCG, Restaurant Chains, Fresh Produce, Ready to Cook Food, Healthcare/Pharma, Meat, Poultry & Seafood, and E-commerce.
- Quality/compliance positioning: "stringent quality management system with periodic audits and real time temperature monitoring", with the deck listing ISO 22000, SGS, BRC certifications, FSSAI License, Good Distribution Practices, Food Safety and Environment Management Systems, and 4 EIA-certified warehouses.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Parent] Snowman is a subsidiary of Gateway Distriparks Limited, which acquired its majority stake in 2006.
- [Technology stack] Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central runs ERP/WMS across operations, warehousing, finance, CRM, supply chain, analytics and warehouse MIS, alongside a transport management system, order management system, complaint ticketing, mobile app-based checklists, digital locks on chambers/vehicles, online chamber monitoring with alerts, IoT-based vehicle monitoring and a 24x7 command centre.
- [Operating environment] Management describes the quarter as "a challenging operating environment due to geo political situation", while pointing to "strategic investments in expanding cold chain infrastructure, enhancing network capacity, and strengthening our integrated logistics solutions" and expecting seasonal demand to strengthen.
- [Leadership] Commentary is attributed to Mr. Padamdeep Singh Handa, CEO & Whole-time director.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Snowman operates a pan-India network of company-owned and build-to-suit temperature-controlled warehouses supported by a fleet of refrigerated vehicles, serving customers across dairy, frozen foods, poultry, seafood, quick-service restaurants, pharmaceuticals and healthcare. The Company reports its business under three reportable segments: Warehousing Services, Transportation Services, and Trading and Distribution. It is a subsidiary of Gateway Distriparks Limited (GDL), which itself operates rail-linked Inland Container Depots and Container Freight Stations for inter-modal EXIM logistics.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Warehousing Services:** temperature-controlled warehousing, dry warehousing
- **Transportation Services:** refrigerated transportation, last-mile distribution, part cargo consolidation, point-to-point full truckload (FTL) services
- **Trading and Distribution:** trading and distribution services
- **Value-Added Services:** blast freezing, kitting, labelling, sorting, repacking, Fifth Party Logistics (5PL), 3PL services

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Snowman targeting INR 1,000 Cr by FY29 (deferred from FY28); Margin: Targeting 15% blended EBITDA at scale; Order Inflow: Domestic rail volumes increasing month-on-month; Capex: Snowman FY27 guide INR 50 Cr (BTS + vehicles); Gateway FY27-28 INR 225 Cr (Indore land balance, Jaipur potential, 3 rakes, EV fleet).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A for logistics services; however, committed volume growth via ArcelorMittal steel coil tender at Ankleshwar MMLP and ramping domestic rail contracts.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Ankleshwar MMLP ramp-up (steel coils); Indore ICD (commencement 2028); Jaipur ICD (legal hearing July 2026); DFC-JNPT last-mile completion (expected in 1 month) unlocking 6k-10k TEUs/month LCL potential; Conversion of dry storage to frozen high-yield cargo.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue to expand in both existing and new markets, with greater use of asset-light, build-to-suit facilities to grow faster and earn satisfactory returns.
- Change the mix between owned and leased facilities — continue investing in owned infrastructure at strategic locations while increasingly adding fully leased and Built-to-Suit facilities to enter new markets faster with lower capital commitment.
- Transition select transportation engagements to an integrated 5PL model.
- Preserve hygiene, safety, reliability and service standards while expanding, so as not to dilute the reputation the business has been built on.
- Strengthen the green logistics portfolio by adopting carbon-neutral operations and investing in sustainable infrastructure.
- Expand multimodal offerings and freight forwarding capabilities to benefit from cost-effective, efficient logistics solutions domestically and internationally.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26, Snowman commissioned four new warehousing facilities — at Kolkata, Krishnapatnam, Kundli (NCR) and Jaipur — adding approximately 17,000 pallet positions, taking total installed pallet capacity to 154,319. The Company has further announced plans to add approximately 22,000 pallets of new capacity at Pune, Patna and Hyderabad, developed on an asset-light basis. The Company continues to pursue an asset-light, build-to-suit (BTS) led expansion strategy, identifying strategic land parcels across key locations to strengthen its national footprint while preserving capital efficiency and operational flexibility; this approach is expected to remain central to the Company's growth strategy going forward.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Continuing formalisation and modernisation of India's cold-chain logistics industry.
- Rising organised food retail, growth in frozen and ready-to-eat food consumption.
- Expansion of pharmaceutical and healthcare distribution.
- Scale-up of quick-commerce and online grocery.
- Asset-light, build-to-suit expansion model expected to enable calibrated capacity addition in line with committed demand while supporting margin improvement over time.
- Rapid growth in Tier 2 and 3 cities, supported by government initiatives and e-commerce expansion, driving demand for scalable and customized logistics services.
- Rise of digital retail and omnichannel strategies increasing need for quick, reliable last-mile delivery and express logistics.
- Customers increasingly willing to pay a premium for assured quality, reliability and compliance versus fragmented unorganised alternatives.
- Warehouses operated at utilisation levels around 86 percent, reflecting strength of demand across the network.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Snowman faces near-term margin pressure from new facility ramp-ups and power costs despite 86-87% utilization, while parent Gateway navigates geopolitical volume headwinds with a strategic pivot to domestic rail and delayed greenfield ICDs (Indore/Jaipur). The INR 1,000 crore revenue target for Snowman is deferred to FY29, shifting the growth narrative from aggressive expansion to operational optimization and asset right-sizing.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Snowman Logistics Limited is India's leading integrated cold chain logistics service provider, offering temperature-controlled and dry warehousing, refrigerated transportation, Fifth Party Logistics (5PL) and supply chain management services.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Snowman operates a pan-India network of company-owned and build-to-suit temperature-controlled warehouses supported by a fleet of refrigerated vehicles, serving customers across dairy, frozen foods, poultry, seafood, quick-service restaurants, pharmaceuticals and healthcare. The Company reports its business under three reportable segments: Warehousing Services, Transportation Services, and Trading and Distribution. It is a subsidiary of Gateway Distriparks Limited (GDL), which itself operates rail-linked Inland Container Depots and Container Freight Stations for inter-modal EXIM logistics.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Gateway Distriparks Limited (GDL) — related party: Holding Company (w.e.f. December 24, 2024); was the investing party in respect of which Snowman was an associate till December 23, 2024. GDL provides inter-modal logistics with rail-linked Inland Container Depots, Container Freight Stations, and a fleet of trains and trailers.
- Gateway Distriparks (Kerala) Limited (GDKL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Star Data Infra and Services Private Limited (SDISPL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence (till March 12, 2025).
- Container Gateway Limited (CGL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Kashipur Infrastructure and Freight Terminal Private Limited (KIFTPL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Prism International Private Limited (PIPL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Perfect Communication Private Limited (PCL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Newsprint Trading and Sales Corporation (NTSC) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Star Cineplex Private Limited (SCPL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.
- Rocksolid Enterprises Private Limited (REPL) — related party: Entity in which directors/investing party/holding company have control or significant influence.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Rail: 96k TEUs (Q4), 40% double-stack coefficient; CFS: 91k TEUs (Q4), volumes subdued due to West Asia; Cold Storage: 160k pallet capacity (market leader), 86-87% utilization, dry storage reduced to <10% mix to improve yields; Transportation: 250 owned + 200 leased vehicles, under margin stress.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Warehousing Services:** temperature-controlled warehousing, dry warehousing
- **Transportation Services:** refrigerated transportation, last-mile distribution, part cargo consolidation, point-to-point full truckload (FTL) services
- **Trading and Distribution:** trading and distribution services
- **Value-Added Services:** blast freezing, kitting, labelling, sorting, repacking, Fifth Party Logistics (5PL), 3PL services

order_book.body: N/A for logistics services; however, committed volume growth via ArcelorMittal steel coil tender at Ankleshwar MMLP and ramping domestic rail contracts.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Snowman targeting INR 1,000 Cr by FY29 (deferred from FY28); Margin: Targeting 15% blended EBITDA at scale; Order Inflow: Domestic rail volumes increasing month-on-month; Capex: Snowman FY27 guide INR 50 Cr (BTS + vehicles); Gateway FY27-28 INR 225 Cr (Indore land balance, Jaipur potential, 3 rakes, EV fleet).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Ankleshwar MMLP ramp-up (steel coils); Indore ICD (commencement 2028); Jaipur ICD (legal hearing July 2026); DFC-JNPT last-mile completion (expected in 1 month) unlocking 6k-10k TEUs/month LCL potential; Conversion of dry storage to frozen high-yield cargo.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continuing formalisation and modernisation of India's cold-chain logistics industry.
- Rising organised food retail, growth in frozen and ready-to-eat food consumption.
- Expansion of pharmaceutical and healthcare distribution.
- Scale-up of quick-commerce and online grocery.
- Asset-light, build-to-suit expansion model expected to enable calibrated capacity addition in line with committed demand while supporting margin improvement over time.
- Rapid growth in Tier 2 and 3 cities, supported by government initiatives and e-commerce expansion, driving demand for scalable and customized logistics services.
- Rise of digital retail and omnichannel strategies increasing need for quick, reliable last-mile delivery and express logistics.
- Customers increasingly willing to pay a premium for assured quality, reliability and compliance versus fragmented unorganised alternatives.
- Warehouses operated at utilisation levels around 86 percent, reflecting strength of demand across the network.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Warehousing margins hit by Kolkata/Krishnapatnam start-up phase and high diesel generator (DG) costs; Transportation segment under constant stress; Employee costs up 12-13% due to pre-hiring for domestic scale-up and retention bonuses; Power cost volatility cited as key margin risk.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt repayment priority (Gateway gross debt down significantly); Dividend continuation; Organic capex for fleet modernization (EV) and terminal expansion; No near-term plans to increase stake in Snowman.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, Snowman commissioned four new warehousing facilities — at Kolkata, Krishnapatnam, Kundli (NCR) and Jaipur — adding approximately 17,000 pallet positions, taking total installed pallet capacity to 154,319. The Company has further announced plans to add approximately 22,000 pallets of new capacity at Pune, Patna and Hyderabad, developed on an asset-light basis. The Company continues to pursue an asset-light, build-to-suit (BTS) led expansion strategy, identifying strategic land parcels across key locations to strengthen its national footprint while preserving capital efficiency and operational flexibility; this approach is expected to remain central to the Company's growth strategy going forward.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic long-term, defensive short-term; Acknowledges 'wait-and-watch' on geopolitics; Transparent on margin headwinds being temporary (ramp-up phase); Committed to asset creation despite demand lull.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: pan-India cold chain network spanning 45 warehouses in 21 cities that lets customers use Snowman as a single national platform rather than multiple regional providers — evidence: '45 warehouses across 21 cities with approximately 1.54 lakhs pallet capacity'; 'this network has taken many years to build and gives us a position that is difficult to replicate'
- licence/regulatory: certifications enabling handling of stringent temperature-sensitive categories such as pharmaceuticals — evidence: 'certified to internationally recognized GFSI standards, including BRCGS, FSSC 22000, and ISO 22000 for food safety and quality management' and 'ISO 14001 certification for our Environmental Management System'

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical tension (West Asia) suppressing EXIM volumes; Delay in DFC-JNPT last-mile connectivity; Regulatory/Legal delays for Jaipur ICD; Power tariff volatility impacting cold storage margins; Execution risk on domestic rail pivot.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Snowman is actively reducing dry storage mix (currently 9-10%) to replace with higher-yield frozen cargo, which should structurally lift ASPs and margins once complete; The 'trading' segment is the sole driver of revenue growth but dilutes overall margins; Gateway is preparing for domestic rail dominance by absorbing upfront empty haulage costs now to secure future market share.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to expand in both existing and new markets, with greater use of asset-light, build-to-suit facilities to grow faster and earn satisfactory returns.
- Change the mix between owned and leased facilities — continue investing in owned infrastructure at strategic locations while increasingly adding fully leased and Built-to-Suit facilities to enter new markets faster with lower capital commitment.
- Transition select transportation engagements to an integrated 5PL model.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Parent] Snowman is a subsidiary of Gateway Distriparks Limited, which acquired its majority stake in 2006.
- [Technology stack] Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central runs ERP/WMS across operations, warehousing, finance, CRM, supply chain, analytics and warehouse MIS, alongside a transport management system, order management system, complaint ticketing, mobile app-based checklists, digital locks on chambers/vehicles, online chamber monitoring with alerts, IoT-based vehicle monitoring and a 24x7 command centre.
- [Operating environment] Management describes the quarter as "a challenging operating environment due to geo political situation", while pointing to "strategic investments in expanding cold chain infrastructure, enhancing network capacity, and strengthening our integrated logistics solutions" and expecting seasonal demand to strengthen.
- [Leadership] Commentary is attributed to Mr. Padamdeep Singh Handa, CEO & Whole-time director.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
